issue_title: Regression in 9.0.1 from 8.33.0 - No longer dedents inputs.
issue_body:
Running `ipython` in the terminal if I copy and paste this block of code:

```python
    # Comment
    x = 1
```

with the leading indentation on both lines, in 8.33.0 it works fine. IPython recognizes the code has consistent leading whitespace, presumably dedents it under the hood, and executes it.

```python
In [1]:     # Comment
   ...:     x = 1

In [2]: 
```

However, in 9.0.1

```python
In [1]:     # Comment
   ...:     x = 1
   ...: 
  Cell In[1], line 2
    x = 1
    ^
IndentationError: unexpected indent

```

I'm not sure if this was intentional or not, but this is a major usability issue for me. My entire workflow is based around copy/pasting chunks of code. I've been working this way for 15 years. I've [written libraries](https://github.com/Erotemic/vimtk) around it. There is a [PR awaiting merge](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103998) in CPython to add this dedent feature to "python -c". 

If this is intentional, I beg the maintainers to reconsider. Otherwise, this is a major bug.

Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 on CPython 3.13.2 and 3.11.2

hints_text:
This is not intentional.

I'm not sure I'll have the time to bisect though.
I can help with that. 

The bad commit is: 2d3f2c619d8ad56a41e3d31f41526d28ab999b56

I will see if it is an easy fix.

Interestingly the indentation needs to start with a comment for the bug to trigger:

```
# This works
ipython -c "
    x = 1
    print(x)
    "

# But this raises an error 
ipython -c "
    # Hello World
    x = 1
    print(x)
    "
```

The offending MR is: https://github.com/ipython/ipython/pull/14721 and corresponding issue is: https://github.com/ipython/ipython/issues/14242

Looking into this, it looks that the test added in the offending MR isn't being run correctly: https://github.com/ipython/ipython/blob/main/tests/test_inputtransformer2_line.py#L185

They define a new test case, but don't actually test it.
